33 A torch uses three lamps connected in parallel and is powered by a cell of electromotive force
(e.m.f.) 3.0 V and negligible internal resistance. Each lamp dissipates 0.60 W of power.
What is the current in the cell?
A
0.067 A
B
0.20 A
C
0.60 A
D
0.83 A

hints: Notice the wording three lamps connected in parallel and each lamp dissipates $0.60\text{ W}$ - the cell must supply power to all three.
Recall that in parallel each lamp has the full $3.0\text{ V}$ across it, and for each lamp $P = VI$ links $0.60\text{ W}$, $3.0\text{ V}$ and its branch current.
First find the current in one lamp from $I = P/V$, then add the three equal branch currents to get the current in the cell.
walkthrough: The cell e.m.f. is $3.0\text{ V}$ with negligible internal resistance, so the terminal p.d. is $3.0\text{ V}$ and each parallel lamp has $V = 3.0\text{ V}$ across it.
For one lamp, use $P = VI$ and rearrange to $I = P/V$.
By Kirchhoff's current law, the current in the cell is the sum of the three parallel branch currents: $I_{cell} = 3 \times 0.20\text{ A}$.
Hence $I_{cell} = 0.60\text{ A}$ with unit $\text{A}$, matching the total-power check $P_{total} = 1.80\text{ W} = 3.0 \times 0.60$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is about one-third of the current in one lamp, found from $0.20/3$. The cell current is the sum of the three parallel branch currents, not a further division.

B.explanation: This is the current in one lamp only, from $I = P/V = 0.60/3.0 = 0.20\text{ A}$. The cell must supply this current to all three parallel lamps.

C.explanation: Total power is $3 \times 0.60 = 1.80\text{ W}$ at $3.0\text{ V}$, so cell current $I = P/V = 1.80/3.0 = 0.60\text{ A}$.

D.explanation: This value does not satisfy $P = VI$ for the total $1.80\text{ W}$ supplied at $3.0\text{ V}$. It is larger than the sum of the three $0.20\text{ A}$ branch currents.
